title: Efficient Electrocatalytic Water Oxidation by Using Amorphous Ni-Co Double Hydroxides Nanocages

lanes.label: Microscopy: SEM, TEM
lanes.sub: foundation model in hand or candidate

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: The Ni/Co ratio in amorphous Ni-Co hydroxide sets surface O* reactivity and thereby OER activity.
states.detail: Need: an efficient, stable, earth-abundant OER catalyst in alkaline media. Gap: why activity varies with metal ratio across double hydroxides is unexplained. Design: seven compositions from Ni(OH)2 to Co(OH)2, hollow nanocages templated on Cu2O by Na2S2O3 etching, and solid ~10 nm particles as the architecture control. Figure 1 is the synthesis schematic.

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Hollow ~80 nm cages with a ~15 nm rough amorphous shell, composition NiCo2.7(OH)x, both metals divalent.
states.detail: Three claims sit here: cage morphology (s1), amorphous state (s2), composition and valence (s3). Microscopy resolves the first. SAED, EDS, XPS and EXAFS resolve the second and third.

states.title: Reactivity state and mechanism
states.head: O* binding energy is non-monotonic in Co content and peaks near 67% Co. O* adsorption is rate-determining, so composition acts through reactivity.
states.detail: The computed descriptor (r1) and the paper's mechanism (m1). Premises: O* binding reported as the OER rate-determining step in earlier work (k3), with the Sabatier caveat that stronger binding can impede O-O bond making (k4). Figure 5 draws composition to reactivity to activity and labels the last link 'deduction'.

states.title: Activity and performance state
states.head: OER activity is a volcano in Co content peaking at 73% Co. eta10 = 0.35 V and 10 h stability at 10 mA cm-2 through the 4e- path.
states.detail: Property r2, performance f1 and f2, and the architecture claim m2 that cages add activity beyond composition (hollow eta10 0.36 V against solid 0.39 V, text only).

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Amorphous NiCo2.7(OH)x cages are efficient and stable because the Ni/Co ratio maximizes O* binding.
states.detail: Supported by f1, f2 and m1. The comparison node x1 places the catalyst beside reported transition-metal catalysts, with NiFe-GO LDH still better at eta10 = 0.21 V.

nodes.title: SEM, Figure 2a
nodes.head: Measures cage size and surface texture: rough spheroids 50 to 105 nm, mostly 70 to 85 nm.
nodes.solves: Size and roughness in the structure state.
nodes.fm: BNL SEM foundation model (ViT-L masked autoencoder with mixture of experts, 125k images). Needs a task head for size distribution and texture.
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure evidence for cage size and roughness, but the structure state is off the path to the conclusion. The composition line never touches morphology.

nodes.title: TEM, Figure 2b, c
nodes.head: Shows the shells are hollow: dark 12 to 15 nm rim around a light core, a ~40 nm cavity in a 70 nm cage.
nodes.solves: Hollowness in the structure state, which SEM cannot see.
nodes.fm: Candidates: EM-DINO (EM-5M), the EMCF corpus, SAM based zero-shot segmentation. Control arm: DINOv2 or DINOv3 with a linear probe.
nodes.note: Outlines are rounded or ovoid rather than the faceted rhombus drawn in Figure 1.
nodes.necessity_reason: Only evidence for hollowness. Feeds the architecture branch alone, whose hollow-versus-solid data are text only.

nodes.title: TEM audit, Figure 2b
nodes.head: The field shows flaky sheet debris and dark collapsed particles between cages. The text says the product is exclusively high-quality nanocages.
nodes.solves: Qualifies the structure state. The figure contradicts the text.
nodes.fm: Same candidates as TEM. A debris-present classifier on the embedding is the cleanest test item in this paper.
nodes.necessity_reason: Dormant. Activity is per geometric area with no ECSA, so debris could change the intrinsic-activity claim. The paper never makes that link.

nodes.title: TEM after 10 h (text only)
nodes.head: The paper says the cages keep shape, size and amorphous state after 10 h. The image sits in the supplement, outside the packet.
nodes.solves: Stability in the activity state, as a text claim only.
nodes.fm: Becomes a TEM item once the supplementary image is pulled in.
nodes.necessity_reason: Text only. Stability stands on the CA and CP curves.

nodes.title: DFT, Figure 4a, b
nodes.head: A NixCo(3-x)O6H6 cluster with an O* adsorbate. O* binding at 0, 33, 67, 100% Co: 4.21, 4.87, 6.17, 5.09 eV.
nodes.solves: The descriptor in the reactivity state.
nodes.fm: A universal MLIP (UMA, MACE-MPA-0, MatterSim, Orb-v3) can re-relax the clusters and add the missing 50, 85 and 90% points, with a DFT single point as the check. A radical O* on a charged hydroxide cluster sits at the edge of their training data.
nodes.necessity_reason: Only support for the reactivity state, and the conclusion's 'because' clause cannot be stated without it.

nodes.title: Bridge audit, Figure 3b x Figure 4b
nodes.head: The reactivity to activity link rests on a rank match over four shared compositions. DFT peaks at 67% Co, the measurement at 73%, and 50, 85, 90% have no DFT counterpart.
nodes.solves: Qualifies the mechanism. A four-point rank match cannot separate a monotonic from a volcano relation.
nodes.fm: Filling the DFT gap with a universal MLIP turns this audit into a counterfactual item: does the completed computed curve still rank the measured one?
nodes.necessity_reason: Shows the necessary DFT link is a four-point rank match, so it is necessary but not sufficient.

nodes.title: Classical, Figure 2c to h
nodes.panel: F2c inset, F2d, F2e, F2f to h
nodes.head: SAED: diffuse halo, no rings. EDS: Co 10.84, Ni 3.99 at% (1:2.72). XPS: 2p splittings 17.6 and 16.1 eV with satellites. EXAFS: N about 5, text only.
nodes.detail: SAED on the cages shows a diffuse halo and no Bragg rings, so the shells are amorphous. The EDS table gives Co 10.84 and Ni 3.99 at%, a 1:2.72 ratio, and the line scan shows Co and Ni rising at both walls with Co about twice Ni. XPS puts Ni 2p3/2 at 856.1 eV and Co 2p3/2 at 781.3 eV, with 17.6 and 16.1 eV splittings and strong satellites, so both metals are divalent. EXAFS coordination numbers near 5 against 6 in crystalline references appear only in the text.
nodes.solves: Phase, composition and valence in the structure state.
nodes.op: recognize signature, convert to quantity, assign features
nodes.inner_audit: The EDS spectrum's tallest peak is Cu with S beside it. The formula names only Ni and Co, and the at% table omits Cu, S, O and C.
nodes.fm: No foundation model. Line-library lookup, NMF unmixing and reference splittings do this exactly.
nodes.necessity_reason: Composition and valence carry the whole composition line.

nodes.title: Electrochemistry, Figure 3
nodes.head: LSV: volcano in j at 1.60 V, 17.8 mA cm-2 at 73% Co. Tafel 65 mV/dec. eta10 0.35 V at 1.58 V. 10 h CA and CP. RRDE: FE 0.98 to 0.99, ~2% peroxide.
nodes.detail: The LSV curves and the current density at 1.60 V give the volcano in Co content, 17.8 mA cm-2 at 73% Co. Tafel slopes fall from 182 to 65 mV/dec at 73% Co. The NiCo2.7 curve crosses 10 mA cm-2 near 1.58 V, so eta10 is 0.35 V. Chronoamperometry and chronopotentiometry hold for 10 h with a slight improvement. The rotating ring-disk data give an O2 Faradaic efficiency of 0.98 to 0.99 with about 2% peroxide, which closes the charge balance for the 4e- path.
nodes.op: read trend, fit model, read characteristic point, compare coplotted quantities
nodes.inner_audit: The stated 1.48 V onset is not resolvable on Figure 3a's 0 to 20 mA cm-2 axis. The curves leave the baseline gradually between 1.47 and 1.52 V.
nodes.fm: No foundation model for polarization curves. Tafel fits, characteristic points and the ring-disk charge balance are classical and verifiable.
